finding.claim: Path traversal in /dl lets an unauthenticated client read arbitrary files readable by the process (e.g. /etc/passwd) via ../ sequences in query parameter f.
finding.sink: os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)) at files.go:13; bytes written to response at files.go:18

trace.note: Attacker-controlled 'f' read from request query with no validation
filepath.Join("/srv/files", f) calls Clean, which resolves '..' so the path can leave root; f=../../../../etc/passwd resolves to /etc/passwd
os.ReadFile succeeds and file contents are written to the HTTP response

finding.guards_checked: None present: no rejection of '..', no filepath.Rel/prefix check against root, no FileServer sandboxing, no authentication. Absolute paths do not escape (Join concatenates under root) but relative traversal does.

verdict.guard_found: none. files.go:12 reads 'f' raw; files.go:13 passes filepath.Join(root, name) straight to os.ReadFile with no '..' rejection or filepath.Rel/prefix check against root; files.go:18 writes the bytes to the response. No authentication on the /dl route registered at files.go:32. The avatar handler's filepath.Base (files.go:22) does not apply to download.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: filepath.Join("/srv/files", "../../../../etc/passwd") cleans to /etc/passwd (files.go:13), the anonymous /dl route (files.go:32) has no guard, and the contents are returned (files.go:18). Note the server listens on :8082 (files.go:34), so the finding is reachable over the network.

finding.claim: /dl and /avatar have no authentication or authorization, and the server listens in plaintext on all interfaces, so any network client can read any file under /srv/files, including non-public data.
finding.source: Any unauthenticated HTTP request reaching port 8082
finding.sink: Protected file contents under /srv/files via download (files.go:13-18)

trace.note: /dl registered on default mux with no middleware
/avatar registered on default mux with no middleware
download handler performs no identity, session, or ownership check
ListenAndServe on ":8082" binds all interfaces over plain HTTP

finding.guards_checked: No auth middleware, no session or identity check, no per-file ACL, no TLS, listen address is not restricted to 127.0.0.1. Impact depends on what is stored under /srv/files, which is not visible in this code.

verdict.guard_found: none. /dl (files.go:32) and /avatar (files.go:33) are registered on the default mux with no middleware. download (files.go:11-18) reads the `f` query value with no identity, session, or ownership check. There is no path containment check: filepath.Join(root, name) at files.go:13 accepts `..` segments. ListenAndServe(":8082") at files.go:34 binds all interfaces over plain HTTP. The avatar handler (files.go:22) applies filepath.Base, but that only narrows the /avatar route and does not affect /dl.
verdict.reason: All cited lines exist and match the trace (files.go:11, 13-18, 32-34), and no auth, ACL, or path-containment check sits between an anonymous network client and os.ReadFile at files.go:13, so any unauthenticated client can read whatever /srv/files holds. The claim understates the scope: because the name is not confined to root, `..` traversal at files.go:13 can also reach files outside /srv/files, so impact is at least what the candidate states.

finding.claim: Possible stored XSS: download writes file bytes without Content-Type or nosniff, so an uploaded HTML or SVG file under /srv/files could be sniffed and executed on the server origin. Conditional on an upload path not present in this code.
finding.source: Contents of files under /srv/files (would be attacker-uploaded in the wider system)
finding.sink: w.Write(data) at files.go:18 with no Content-Type or X-Content-Type-Options header

trace.note: Bytes written with no explicit Content-Type and no nosniff header, so the browser may sniff HTML/SVG

finding.guards_checked: No Content-Type set, no X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, no Content-Disposition. No upload handler exists in files.go to confirm attacker control of file contents.

verdict.guard_found: none. files.go:18 has no Content-Type or X-Content-Type-Options header and no Content-Disposition. The only checks are the os.ReadFile error path at files.go:14-17, which affect only the 404 response. Note that net/http auto-sniffs Content-Type on the first Write when none is set, so the browser-sniffing premise is incomplete, though the XSS mechanism would still apply to HTML content.
verdict.reason: Lines files.go:13 and files.go:18 match the trace, but the attacker-controlled content the finding depends on is not written anywhere in this code, and the upload path that would supply it is absent, so the finding cannot be confirmed or refuted from the available code.
